Hi Carlos / Alicia — copying short answers to help your intake team. Happy to expand on any row in the questionnaire.

1) SOC 2 scope: Our SOC 2 Type II covers the Redwood hosted control plane and the inference runtime used for hosted customers. Dedicated pools and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem packages) are in-scope when included in customer-specific attestations — we can provide specifics in the report.

2) Multi-tenant hardware: Hosted shared pools are multi-tenant but we use strict isolation at the runtime and container level and do not share per-tenant KV caches or persistent storage. Dedicated pools are single-customer.

3) CMK behavior in hosted mode: When customers choose customer-managed keys (CMK), we never persist unwrapped key material in our persistent storage. The CMK is used for envelope encryption: Redwood requests short-lived wrapping keys from the KMS to encrypt per-model or per-tenant object keys; unwrapped master keys do not persist and are only handled inside HSM/KMS boundaries.

4) HSM support: We support AWS KMS + CloudHSM-backed keys, GCP KMS with HSM-backed keys, and integrations with customer HSM/Vault via KMIP or external key proxy (for Private deployments). For on-prem air-gapped installs we support customer-supplied HSM modules (FIPS 140-2/3 certified) via the Private package.

5) TLS & in-transit: All traffic to our hosted API uses TLS 1.3. Internal service-to-service communication in Hosted uses mTLS. For Private deployments, TLS termination can be customer-controlled in the VPC.

6) Rotation cadence: By default we rotate ephemeral data keys frequently (hours); CMKs are rotated per-customer policy and can be automated via KMS rotation or customer rotation.

We'll fill out the attached spreadsheet with these short answers and return by EOD tomorrow. If you need the SOC 2 report under NDA, please send the NDA link or DocuSign form.

Best,
Priyom
Security & Trust Engineer | Redwood Inference
